newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish coalition moves to reconciliation.
newsitem.headline: Polish coalition moves to reconciliation.

text.p: Poland's two leftist ruling parties appeared on Thursday to be overcoming a deadlock over a coming cabinet reorganisation and proposed candidates to head a key new treasury ministry.

The smaller Polish Peasant Party (PSL) agreed that the cabinet reshuffle should involve a gradual replacement of individual ministers rather than the dismissal of the whole cabinet and a prompt formation of a new one.

The issue has so far deeply divided the PSL and the larger ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD), whose rift had recently been aggravated when SLD's prime minister sacked a Peasant official from the cabinet without consultations.
"For now the appointment in the treasury ministry is the main problem," PAP news agency quoted Agriculture Minister and a Peasant leader Roman Jagielinski as saying.
SLD leader Jozef Oleksy said Wieslaw Kaczmarek, whose privatisation ministry is to be replaced by a more powerful treasury portfolio in October, should remain in charge.
But Oleksy also praised the Peasant candidate for the ministry, Planning Minister Miroslaw Pietrewicz. "We think it is not a bad candidate," PAP quoted him as saying.

Oleksy said his party should control ministries of treasury and interior, while the Peasant party should appoint the heads of a large new economy ministry and of the Strategic Research Centre, due to replace the planning ministry.
Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko should keep his post because his portfolio was not much affected by the reform, due to begin in October and spread over many months, Olesky added.
The cabinet reform, under which seven ministries are to be liquidated and several new created, is meant to streamline government's decision-making and reduce its role in the economy.
